commenti.body:
I don’t think it’s your attention span, I think the prevalence of streaming platforms has indulged filmmakers in the worst ways, because previously there were fairly strict ideas on how long a studio would allow a film to be to maximise how many showings they could get in a single theatre per day.

Likewise, TV shows used to live and die by the strict time limits of commercial TV slots, whereas nowadays a typical “half-hour” drama/comedy can easily run 45-55 mins long per episode.

I think in some instances, this can be for the best, but the vast majority of media these days is way longer than it needs to be, because filmmakers are no longer having to hone scripts and edits to be as tight as possible.

Especially for things like genre fair, I feel like short and punchy is way more effective than long and drawn out. I honestly thought The Substance would’ve been vastly better and *more* shocking had it lost 30-40 mins from its runtime, because honestly the plot is so simplistic and threadbare that there’s not enough to sustain the run time on shock and awe (and closeups of Qualley’s butt) alone.

Even a lot of “epic” stories like Killers of the Flower Moon I thought took its sweet time through the whole middle section so much so that I got bored, despite its overall quality as a film.

I honestly miss the day of a tight 90-100 min film that doesn’t fuck about and just keeps you engaged with every second.

yeah the average film length is ridiculous now and you can really see it in kid’s stuff. my daughter wanted to watch the live action dumbo last week and it was 2 hours long! the og dumbo is like 80 minutes. it seems to me that most movies hit the 2 hour mark now where 90 mins would suffice.

To me it feels like a little bit of both. I find myself going to look at my phone out of habit, even if I’m engaged with the movie I’m watching. Sometimes it’s so bad I have to physically put my phone on the other side of the room. But, I do think runtimes have gotten a little excessive. I’ve noticed with a lot of new movies that pacing does not seem to be a primary focus for the filmmakers. I feel like most movies could shave off ten minutes or so and be better for it.

Yes, I'd say your attention span isn't keeping up. Which, in my experience, is usually a sign that you'd rather be doing something else.

Maybe take a break from watching movies? Go for a hike. Take a swim. Have a drink. Spend a couple of weeks doing things other than watching movies.

I’m not sure it’s fair to say that very long films are a product of streaming, or a new phenomenon . All those mid century roadshow epics were long enough to necessitate an intermission. 

The runtimes of David Lean’s last five films, for instance, are 161 minutes, 227 minutes, 193 minutes, 195 minutes and 163 minutes. 

Titanic, once the highest grossing film of all time, is 195 minutes long. Another film that held that title for decades, Gone with the Wind, is about 4 hours long in its roadshow version. Once Upon a Time in America is longer still.

Surviving cuts of Intolerance are more than 3 hours long. 

I could keep adding examples but I think you get the point. The epic length film has been part of cinema for more than a century.

For sure. A lot of the time even for good movies, when I can tell it’s wrapping up, there’s a scene where I’m like “wow, that’s a fitting ending” and then it just keeps going because you have to show what happens to each character and how every family member reacts to their return or the like…

As much as people don't like to admit it, attention spans have 100% gone down. I know many film lovers in my circle who used to watch multiple movies each week. Now they watch maybe 1 in a week or two and find it hard to stay focused.

I think a 2 hour length for a movie is pretty reasonable. Always has been. When an episode of TV can go on for an hour, a movie going on for 2 hours is no issue at all.

More than 2 hours is when one can start questioning the purpose of the timing, but as long as the story demands it, and the direction is such that it keeps you engaged, I see no harm in it at all.

The original Dumbo is actually 64 minutes, but is a bizarre movie that feels like an extended short. It’s important to remember the movie basically ends like right after he learns to fly. The new Dumbo for all its faults is the same basic story as the original and basically a sequel to that story.
